RageDroid adds a second layer of encryption to every protected secret. Opening a protected item needs one of your keys -- a YubiKey, a security key, or this phone\'s secure element.
Ragewarden encrypts every item to a recipient you control. Enrol a YubiKey, this phone\'s StrongBox, a passkey, or a paper recovery phrase before saving anything.
Ragewarden is locked, so this keyboard lists nothing until you unlock it.

This passkey wraps items as fido2-hmac, which other clients read as a security-key secret. Moving it makes new wraps webauthn-prf-v1, the passkey format; what it wrapped before keeps opening, and Re-encrypt on an item renews it.
Passkey moved. Re-encrypt items to renew their old wraps.
Tap Start to generate the key in this phone\'s secure element. You\'ll confirm with biometrics if the device has them.
Tap Start, then present your key: insert via USB-C, or hold it to the back of the phone.
Tap Start and enter your PIV PIN, then present the YubiKey: USB-C, or held to the back of the phone.

Each protected item is opened with one tap of your key and written back unchanged, wrapped to the current recipients, so a key you revoked can no longer open it. Items you reveal later are also renewed on their own.
24 words you write down. Works without a network.
This phone has no screen lock

Without a screen lock or fingerprint, a key in this phone opens your protected items with no confirmation at all: anyone holding the unlocked phone can use it. Set a screen lock first, and the key will ask for it on every use.
